one_month_reasoning: Three scheduled events fall in the window: Texas Instruments Q3 results/call on Wed 2026-10-21 (src 31), the first read on analog/industrial demand; NXP Q3 after the close on Tue 2026-10-27 (src 32), STM's closest auto/MCU peer; and STM's own Q3 results and Q4 guide on 2026-10-29 before the European open (src 3, 30). STM's last seven earnings-day moves were -9.0%, +7.2%, -15.9%, -13.3%, -5.6%, +10.8%, -18.7% (Yahoo daily, src 13): mean absolute ~11.6%, 5 of 7 negative. Q3 was guided to $3.70B at 37.0% GM and Q4 'above $4B' (src 2), so the bar is set and the risk is a GM path or Q4 guide that disappoints as in July. Against that, the stock already fell 15.6% from $58.72 (Oct 6) to $49.57, about twice SMH's move (src 13, 14), so short-term reversal offsets weak momentum. With two peer prints plus our own, I widen the spread versus round 1: a 50/50 mix of 13% and 25% monthly sigma (effective ~19%, above 61%/3.5 = 17%) around a median of $49.2, slightly below spot for the negative skew of recent prints. P(>= spot) 0.48.

fair_value.method: Blend of 16x NTM GAAP after-SBC EPS at the horizon (~$3.05, mostly FY2028; $48.87, w 0.6) and a 4-year DCF at 10.8% WACC and 3% terminal growth ($45.68, w 0.4) = $47.59, the engine's base horizon value. Net cash $1,701M (adjusted NFP), 900M shares, tax 17%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM GAAP EPS at 2027-10-13 ~$3.05 (FY2027 revenue $17.2B at 14.5% EBIT, FY2028 $18.6B at 19%, tax 17%, ~897M shares at the horizon) x 16x = $48.87 (engine)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY2027 $17.18B (+19.05%); Barclays $17.35B.

FY2028 ~$18.6B, in line with the 2027-28 intermediate model (~$18B) and the datacenter ramp (well above $2B in 2027); trimmed from round 1's +10%/+6% toward the base rate after analog up-cycles (2023-25 revenue fell from $17.3B to $11.8B, F1/F3) as part of the risk of a 2028 down-cycle.
Barclays: 2027 GM 39.2% x $17.35B = $6.80B less net opex $4.1B = $2.70B (15.6%); less ~1pt for restructuring charges in GAAP = 14.5%.
Barclays sees ~43% GM in 2028; the 2027-28 model targets 22-24% op margin; we haircut 3-4pts for execution/price pressure. FY2023 peak margin was 26.7% (F5/F1).

ST's 2026 estimated annual effective rate is 18.1% incl. 0.5% Pillar Two (Q2 OFR); FY2023 11.4% (541/4,763) and FY2024 16.7% (313/1,878) from the 20-F. With Pillar Two now permanent, 17% sits just below the 2026 guide, allowing a little mix benefit. (Round 1 used 14%.)

Adjusted net financial position $1.70B = NFP $2,007M less $306M advances received on capital grants (Q2 release). The grant advances fund capex not yet spent, and modelled capex is net of grants, so they are excluded.

892.55M shares outstanding (StockAnalysis) plus ~7.5M of unvested-award dilution = ~900M. The Q2 diluted weighted count of 928.0M (Q2 release) also includes if-converted shares from the $750M Tranche B convertible (conversion price $45.10; 750/45.10 = 16.6M shares), whose principal is in financial debt and was due to be settled net-share in Q3 2026 (Q2 OFR). Using 928M with that debt in net debt would count it twice. Cross-check: 928.0 - 16.6 = 911.4M is an upper bound.

Peer median next-FY P/E of my 10 IDM peers 16.56x (range 11.99x Renesas to 27.05x TXN; price / next-FY consensus); peers' adjusted EPS excludes SBC, so like-for-like ~18x. Discount ~3% to the quoted median and ~11% like-for-like, argued from history: at end-2023 STM traded at 11.2x trailing GAAP EPS ($50.13/$4.46) vs TXN 24.1x, NXPI 21.5x, ON 17.1x, ADI 30.3x (median 22.8x); at end-2024 15.0x ($24.97/$1.66) vs TXN 36.1x, NXPI 21.4x, ON 17.4x, ADI 64.8x (median 28.7x): a ~50% discount at both points, from lower margins and higher capital intensity that persist (FY25 GAAP op margin 1.5%, D&A 15.7% of revenue). I take only part of that discount because trailing GAAP multiples at different cycle points are noisy. (Round 1 used 15x.) [citation gate 2026-10-14: rebuilt as 2026-10-13 close / next-FY consensus EPS from each peer's StockAnalysis forecast page, the 10-peer median is 16.56x (range 11.99x Renesas to 27.05x TXN; the 16.9x / 12.4x / 28.0x were Finviz/StockAnalysis aggregator figures); 16x is ~3% below it. The 16x choice is unchanged.]

bear.story: Analog/MCU/auto down-cycle pulled into 2027-28 after the memory-led 2026 boom (SIA Aug sales +144% y/y; base rate: the 2023-25 analog downturn took STM revenue from $17.3B to $11.8B, F1/F3); GM stalls ~37-39%, 2027 revenue ~flat at $14-15B, GAAP EPS ~$1.5-2 at 14-16x, i.e. back below the pre-rerating March 2026 range ($31-35); Barclays worst case EUR30 (~$34) includes Apple content loss. 30% reflects the closest historical setup (>=30% rally then >=30% drawdown: median -14%, 42% up, ~6 episodes) and STM's 5-of-7 negative earnings reactions; prediction-market recession odds are context only.

base.story: Consensus-like path: revenue $14.4B (2026) and ~$17.2B (2027), datacenter well above $2B in 2027, GAAP op margin ~14.5% in 2027 rising to ~19% in 2028; market pays ~16x NTM GAAP after-SBC EPS (~$3.05) at the horizon; adjusted net cash ~$1.7B, 900M shares.

bull.story: Datacenter/satellite/AI-power ramps beat, GM returns to mid-40s and the 22-24% op margin model is reached in 2028; market pays ~20x (peer like-for-like median plus) on ~$3.7 EPS, back toward the June 2026 high ($81).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A persistent discount is shown by history, not asserted: at end-2023 STM traded at 11.2x trailing GAAP EPS vs a 22.8x median for TXN/NXPI/ON/ADI, and at end-2024 at 15.0x vs 28.7x (Yahoo year-end closes, SEC XBRL EPS; src 34, 35, F13, F14), i.e. ~50% below peers at both points. The drivers persist through the horizon: structurally lower margins (FY25 GAAP op margin 1.5%; Q3 GM guide 37% vs high-50s/60s at TXN/NXPI/MCHP), higher capital intensity (net capex at the high end of $2.0-2.2B in 2026, D&A 15.7% of revenue), Apple concentration and SiC/MCU exposure to Chinese competition. I apply only ~11% (like-for-like) because trailing GAAP multiples at different cycle points overstate it; the supervisor's 17x (~6%) is close, but the historical gap argues for slightly more.

thesis_break_reason: $30 is the pre-rerating level of March 2026 (weekly closes $30.86-34.55) before the datacenter target doubled, ~10x the horizon NTM GAAP EPS (~$3.05) and below Barclays' worst case (EUR30 ~ $34 with Apple loss). A close there would mean the market has priced away both the datacenter/satellite growth leg and the gross-margin recovery (2027 revenue near flat, GM stuck <38%), not ordinary 60%-vol noise around a ~$47.6 value. It sits just above my $27 bear value.

reverse_dcf_check: At 10.8% WACC the DCF gives $45.68; the 16x NTM P/E leg ($48.87) is matched by the DCF at a WACC of ~10.3% (engine reverse DCF). So the horizon multiple implies, after 2029, a ~20% GAAP EBIT margin held for good, ~10% of revenue reinvested as capex, and 3% perpetual growth at ~10.3% cost of capital. That is plausible: it is well below STM's 2023 peak margin (26.7%) and its 22-24% through-cycle target, leaving room for the China-competition, Apple and down-cycle risks above; a peer-median-plus multiple (18-20x) would need the 22-24% model and a lower discount rate.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT (after SBC) is used throughout; SBC ($193M in FY2025, ~1.4% of revenue going forward) is an expense, not added back, and the share count falls only ~0.3%/yr. ST's non-GAAP excludes only restructuring/impairment and NXP-MEMS PPA (Q2 release), so its consensus EPS is also after SBC. Peers' consensus EPS excludes SBC, so their quoted P/Es understate the like-for-like multiple by ~5-10%; I benchmark 16x against ~18x like-for-like.

reasoning: Base rates first: STM's own 12-month return since 1997 has a median of ~+1% with a 40% annual sd; pooled analog/semis peers +12.6% (64% up); in the closest setup (>=30% 12-month rally then >=30% drop from the 12-month high, where STM sits after $22->$81->$49.6) the pooled peer median was -14% with 42% up, but only ~6 independent episodes. Per the supervisor, these now shape only the width and skew of the distribution, not fair value (the round-1 anchor leg is dropped). Fundamentals: Q2 revenue +26% y/y, Q3 guide $3.70B/37% GM, Q4 >$4B, datacenter well above $2B in 2027; consensus 2026/27 revenue $14.4B/$17.2B. A GAAP after-SBC model (EBIT margin 8/14.5/19/20% for 2026-29, revenue +22/+19/+8/+5%, tax 17%) valued at 16x NTM EPS (~$3.05) gives $48.87 and a DCF at 10.8% gives $45.68; with adjusted net cash $1,701M and 900M shares the blend is $47.59. The 16x sits ~11% below the like-for-like peer median, supported by STM's ~50% trailing-P/E discount to TXN/NXPI/ON/ADI at end-2023 and end-2024. Scenarios 30/45/25 at $27/$47.6/$74 give a median ~$46.1 and mean ~$49.9; each is spread with 26-32% sigma so the total log-sd is ~0.47, between STM's 10-year (42%) and 1-year (61%) realized vol. Sell-side mean target $75 is noted but not followed. Prediction-market macro odds are context only. Research limits: sec.gov was read with WebFetch; an ASML Q3 date was found only on third-party calendars and is left out.

discount_rate.basis: Cost of equity 11.5% = 10y UST 5.24% (FRED DGS10, 2026-10-09) + beta 1.49 x ERP 4.20% (Damodaran implied ERP, 2026-10-01). Beta: mean of two raw 5y betas, our own monthly regression vs SPY 1.97 (Yahoo, 59 months) and StockAnalysis 5Y 1.48 = 1.725, Blume-adjusted 0.67x1.725+0.33 = 1.49. Debt $4.02B vs $43.78B market cap = 8.4% weight at ~3.5% after tax. WACC = 0.916x11.48% + 0.084x3.5% = 10.8%.

horizon_multiples.peer_basis: Median next-FY P/E of 10 analog/MCU/power IDM peers 16.56x (range 11.99-27.05x, price / next-FY consensus from StockAnalysis forecast pages); ~18x like-for-like since peers exclude SBC. 16x is ~3% below the quoted median and ~11% below like-for-like, inside the range. The 16x choice is unchanged.]

bear.story: 2027-28 analog/MCU/auto down-cycle after the memory-led 2026 boom (base rate: the 2023-25 analog cycle took STM revenue -32%); GM stalls near 37-39%; Apple content loss risk (Barclays worst case EUR30). Recession and rate odds from prediction markets are context only.

base.story: Consensus-like revenue path ($14.4B 2026, ~$17.2B 2027), GAAP operating margin rebuilding to ~19% in 2028 as reshaping savings land; market pays ~16x NTM GAAP EPS (~$3.05).

bull.story: Datacenter revenue well above $2B in 2027 plus satellite/AI power wins, gross margin back to mid-40s, 2027-28 model (22-24% op margin) reached early; market re-rates toward peer median and above.

model_inputs.structure_note: Standard structure fits: integrated device maker with fabs; GAAP EBIT after SBC. Round 1's base-rate anchor custom leg is removed (it was spot x historical drift, not a valuation).
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value equals the engine base horizon value ($47.59). My judgment scenario prices ($27/$47.6/$74) differ from the engine's ($22.7/$47.6/$72.5) because the engine's bear compounds the growth, margin, multiple and WACC hits together, which puts it below the March 2026 trading range ($30.9-34.6) and below STM's 2024 trough-year value; I use $27 instead.

Consensus FY2027 $17.18B (+19.05%); Barclays $17.35B.

FY2028 ~$18.6B, in line with the 2027-28 intermediate model (~$18B) and the datacenter ramp (well above $2B in 2027); trimmed from round 1's +10%/+6% toward the base rate after analog up-cycles (2023-25 revenue fell from $17.3B to $11.8B, F1/F3) as part of the risk of a 2028 down-cycle.

Q1 GAAP op income $70M + Q2 $187M (Q2 release) = $257M. H2 ~$0.90B (agent estimate): Q3 ~$0.34B = guided $3.70B x 37% GM ($1.37B) less ~$1.03B GAAP opex at Q2's level (3,487 x 34.8% - 187 = $1,026M); Q4 ~$0.56B = ~13.5% on the implied Q4 revenue of ~$4.12B ($14.40B - $6.58B H1 - $3.70B Q3; guided 'above $4B'). ($0.257B + $0.90B) / $14.4B = 8.0%. A Q4 margin near Q3's would give ~7.5%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Barclays: 2027 GM 39.2% x $17.35B = $6.80B less net opex $4.1B = $2.70B (15.6%); less ~1pt for restructuring charges in GAAP = 14.5%.
Barclays sees ~43% GM in 2028; the 2027-28 model targets 22-24% op margin; we haircut 3-4pts for execution/price pressure. FY2023 peak margin was 26.7% (F5/F1).

ST's 2026 estimated annual effective rate is 18.1% incl. 0.5% Pillar Two (Q2 OFR); FY2023 11.4% (541/4,763) and FY2024 16.7% (313/1,878) from the 20-F. With Pillar Two now permanent, 17% sits just below the 2026 guide, allowing a little mix benefit. (Round 1 used 14%.)
FY2025 D&A $1,854M / $11,800M = 15.7%; D&A held ~$1.95-2.0B while revenue grows.
Q2 2026 net capex $409M / revenue $3,487M = 11.7%; trending down as reshaping program limits fab spend.
FY2025 SBC $193M / $11,800M = 1.6%; held flat in dollars as revenue grows. Costed in GAAP EBIT.
FY2025 buybacks $367M + dividends $321M = $688M.

Adjusted net financial position $1.70B = NFP $2,007M less $306M advances received on capital grants (Q2 release). The grant advances fund capex not yet spent, and modelled capex is net of grants, so they are excluded.

892.55M shares outstanding (StockAnalysis) plus ~7.5M of unvested-award dilution = ~900M. The Q2 diluted weighted count of 928.0M (Q2 release) also includes if-converted shares from the $750M Tranche B convertible (conversion price $45.10; 750/45.10 = 16.6M shares), whose principal is in financial debt and was due to be settled net-share in Q3 2026 (Q2 OFR). Using 928M with that debt in net debt would count it twice. Cross-check: 928.0 - 16.6 = 911.4M is an upper bound.

Agent judgment, not derived. Diluted shares 944.2M (2023, F16) -> 923.1M (2025, F18) = (923.1/944.2)^0.5 - 1 = -1.1%/yr with ~$367M of FY25 buybacks (F33). -0.3%/yr assumes ~0.8pt a year of offsetting dilution (the 2026 convertible and awards); the facts do not show that much: the Tranche B excess was ~1.6M one-off shares delivered from treasury and the 2031/2033 bonds are far out of the money. On the history alone the figure is about -1%/yr; the supervisor's reconciled set uses -0.5%.
